Collision policy: fail, skip, overwrite, auto-rename (only with --batch; single paths always refuse) -b, --batch Batch process all files in input directory --mode Batch stages (default: auto; only with --batch): auto: archives-(7z)-ISO/dir-.zar, ISOs-.zar, dirs-.zar extract-archive: extract archives with 7z, stop there extract-iso: convert ISOs to .zar; compress: pack directories to .zar --seven-zip 7z binary for th [truncated]

Usage: zar zstd -c|-d [-l N] [--dict <file>] [--check|--no-check] [-q] [input] [output]

Compress or decompress a single zstd stream (not a .zar archive):
  zar zstd -c [in] [out]   Compress (level 6 default)
  zar zstd -d [in] [out]   Decompress

Omitted input reads stdin, omitted output writes stdout, so pipes work:
  zar zstd -c big.bin | zar zstd -d > big.back

Options:
  -c, --compress        Compress (exactly one of -c/-d is required)
  -d, --decompress      Decompress
  -l, --level <N>       Compression level 1-22, compress only (default: 6)
      --dict <file>     Dictionary file (zstd -D semantics: never stored,
                        keep it alongside; required on both sides for dict frames)
      --stdout          Explicit stdout (already the default when no output
                        path is given; an error together with one)
      --check           Write a content checksum (compress only)
      --no-check        Do not write a checksum (default; last flag wins)
  -q, --quiet           Suppress the input -> output line
  -h, --help            Show this help

Note: inside 'zar zstd', -c means --compress (not --stdout).

Usage: zar seekable compress|decompress|list [options] [input] [output] Seekable zstd files (zeekstd-compatible framing: independently compressed frames plus a seek table) — not single-frame 'zar zstd' streams: zar seekable compress [in] [out] Compress to seekable .zst (level 3 default) zar seekable decompress [in] [out] Decompress, whole file or a --from/--to slice zar seekable list Frame summary or per-frame detail table Omitted input reads stdin (compress streams it; decompress buffers it), omitted output writes stdout, so pipes work: zar seekable compress big.bin | zar seekable decompress > big.back Compress options: -l, --level Compression level 1-22 (default: 3) -s, --frame-size New frame every S bytes: 10, 10B, 10K, 10M, 10G (default: 2M; capped at 1G) --frame-size-policy

compressed or uncompressed (default: uncompressed) --checksum Frame checksums (default on; also --check) --no-checksum No frame checksums (also --no-check; last flag wins) --seek-table-file Write a standalone Head table there instead of appending the Foot table (decompress: read the table from there instead of the file tail) Decompress options: --from Start at decompressed byte S (default: 0) --to End at decompressed byte S (default: end) --from-frame Start at frame N (not with --from) --to-frame End after frame N inclusive (not with --to) List options: --from-frame First frame shown (default: 0) --to-frame Last frame shown, inclusive (default: last) --num-frames Frame count shown, >= 1 (not with --to-frame) -d, --detail Per-frame table (implied by frame bounds) --seek-table-format foot reads the appended table (default); head [truncated]
